idea: Unit-bearing boundary assertions as a test-local diagnostic seam
sketch: The repeated repairs cluster around boundaries—manifest entry caps, UTF-8 byte truncation, and Git-status slices—where raw numbers hide whether the test is talking about entries, bytes, or records. Adopt a test-local boundary assertion convention that prints the unit and a short boundary label beside observed and expected values, while retaining the existing direct unittest comparison and exit behavior. A failing message such as `manifest size: expected 512 entries, got 513 entries` or `UTF-8 payload: expected 512 bytes, got 508 bytes` would let both worker and parent identify an expectation-versus-fixture mistake without writing a one-off probe. The convention should be applied only to existing boundary checks after a sourcechecked diagnosis, so it removes repair loops without adding a mandatory stage, parser, ledger, or dependency. Independent acceptance still runs the existing unittest and packaging/build checks, and the enriched messages become evidence rather than a substitute for those checks. This also makes mismatched units visible when a byte limit is accidentally asserted against a character or slice count.
load_bearing_risk: If the real bottleneck is missing runner ownership or a wrong contract rather than ambiguous diagnostics, message-only edits will not reduce repair time; an overgeneralized helper could also obscure the original unittest stack location.
first_concrete_step: Run the existing focused unittest target and inventory the affected boundary assertions, then patch the smallest set of ambiguous messages with explicit units and labels while leaving comparison expressions unchanged.
subideas: Direct-message variant: add literal unit-bearing messages to each existing unittest assertion and avoid any new helper, which is safest if the affected sites are few.
Tiny-helper variant: add one private TestCase helper accepting observed, expected, unit, and label, but delegate to unittest so stack locations and raw exits remain intact.

Stronger-boundary pair: retain exact expected assertions and add a unit-bearing <= cap invariant only where the contract permits, distinguishing fixture size from encoded-byte size without weakening proof.
Failure-routing unlock: use labels to classify failures as fixture, encoding, or repository-state boundaries so a parent can route one repair to its owner instead of repeating probes.
wildcard_question: If the next failing message already named its unit and owner, would the remaining worker-parent loop reveal that the true missing abstraction is runner ownership rather than assertion clarity?
